---
title: "Getting started"
---

This page installs chameleon-rs, renders a template from a string, then sets up a folder of
template files the way a web app would.

## Install

```bash
uv pip install chameleon-rs
```

chameleon-rs supports CPython 3.12 to 3.15, including the free-threaded builds (3.14t,
3.15t). The wheel contains the compiled engine and has no dependencies. The framework
integrations use the framework your app already has, so there are no extras to install.

## Render a template string

`PageTemplate` compiles a template from a string. Calling it renders the template, with the
keyword arguments as the template's variables:

```{python}
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate

page = PageTemplate("""
<div class="greeting">
  <h1>Hello, ${name}!</h1>
  <ul tal:condition="items">
    <li tal:repeat="item items">${repeat.item.number}. ${item}</li>
  </ul>
</div>
""")

print(page(name='World', items=['templates', 'in', 'Rust']))
```

The template compiles once, when it's first rendered. Every later render reuses the compiled
program, so keep template objects around (module level, or in a loader) rather than building
one per request.

`${...}` inserts a value with HTML escaping. To insert markup as-is, use `structure:`, or pass
an object with an `__html__` method:

```{python}
page = PageTemplate('<p>${text}</p> <p>${structure: text}</p>')
print(page(text='<b>bold</b>'))
```

## Render templates from files

`PageTemplateFile` loads one file. `PageTemplateLoader` loads templates by name from one or
more folders, and caches each compiled template:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pathlib, tempfile

folder = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'templates'
(folder / 'home').mkdir(parents=True)
(folder / 'shared').mkdir()
(folder / 'home' / 'index.pt').write_text(
    '<html>\n'
    '  <body>\n'
    '    <h1>${title}</h1>\n'
    '    <div tal:repeat="video videos">\n'
    "      ${render_partial('shared/video.pt', video=video)}\n"
    '    </div>\n'
    '  </body>\n'
    '</html>\n'
)
(folder / 'shared' / 'video.pt').write_text('<a href="/videos/${video.id}">${video.title}</a>')
template_folder = str(folder)
```

Suppose your templates live in a folder like this:

```text
templates/
├── home/
│   └── index.pt
└── shared/
    └── video.pt
```

with `home/index.pt`:

```html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>${title}</h1>
    <div tal:repeat="video videos">
      ${render_partial('shared/video.pt', video=video)}
    </div>
  </body>
</html>
```

and `shared/video.pt`:

```html
<a href="/videos/${video.id}">${video.title}</a>
```

Configure the folder once at startup with `chameleon_rs.configure()`, then load templates by
name:

```{python}
from dataclasses import dataclass

import chameleon_rs
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplateLoader


@dataclass
class Video:
    id: int
    title: str


chameleon_rs.configure(template_folder=template_folder)
templates = PageTemplateLoader([template_folder])

page = templates['home/index.pt']
print(page(title='Latest videos', videos=[Video(1, 'Intro'), Video(2, 'Partials')]))
```

`render_partial` is available in every template, with nothing to register or pass in.
`configure()` tells it where to find partials. See [Partials](partials.qmd).

In a real app, build the folder path relative to your code, so it doesn't depend on the
working directory:

```python
from pathlib import Path

import chameleon_rs

template_folder = Path(__file__).parent / 'templates'
chameleon_rs.configure(template_folder=template_folder, auto_reload=dev_mode)
```

`auto_reload=True` recompiles a template when its file changes. Turn it on in development and
leave it off in production.

## In a web app

In a web app you rarely call templates yourself. The framework integrations configure the
folder and render what your views return:

```python
import fastapi

import chameleon_rs.fastapi as chameleon

app = fastapi.FastAPI()
chameleon.configure(template_folder=template_folder, auto_reload=dev_mode, app=app)


@app.get('/')
@chameleon.template('home/index.pt')
async def index():
    return {'title': 'Latest videos', 'videos': await load_videos()}
```

[Web frameworks](frameworks.qmd) shows the same view in Flask, Quart, FastAPI, Starlette,
Robyn, Litestar and Pyramid, and links to each framework's guide.
